prompt.en: A receiver stage takes a 7 MHz modulated signal and produces a larger voltage at the same frequency with the same modulation. Which block behaviour fits?

feedback.en: The stage raises the existing RF level while preserving frequency and information.
Detection recovers the information as audio. The described output is still modulated RF at 7 MHz.
A frequency-converting mixer moves the signal to another frequency. The described carrier frequency did not change.
An oscillator generates a repeating signal. Here an existing input is being made larger with its modulation preserved.

explanation.en: Gain can apply to RF or audio. Identify the signal type and whether frequency or information changed, not just whether the output grew.

prompt.en: Two amplifiers preserve a test waveform equally well, but one draws more DC power for the same RF output. Which comparison follows?

text.en: The higher-draw amplifier must be more non-linear.

feedback.en: Extra DC draw can mean more wasted heat even when the waveform is equally clean.

text.en: The lower-draw amplifier has less voltage gain even if its RF output is the same.

feedback.en: Efficiency compares power conversion. The observations do not establish a voltage-gain difference.

text.en: Both have equal efficiency because both preserve waveform shape.

feedback.en: Clean shape addresses linearity, not how much DC power is converted to useful output.

text.en: The higher-draw amplifier is less efficient; the test does not show worse linearity.

feedback.en: For equal useful output, more DC input means lower efficiency. The equal waveform quality is separate evidence about linearity.

explanation.en: Judge signal shape and power conversion separately. Clean amplification can still waste considerable heat.

prompt.en: An LED indicator is moved to a higher supply voltage while its series resistor and assumed LED drop stay unchanged. What should be rechecked?

text.en: The greater resistor voltage raises current and heat, so its value and wattage need checking.

feedback.en: The resistor must now drop more voltage. With unchanged resistance, current and power dissipation rise.

text.en: Keep the resistor unchanged if the replacement supply has the same maximum current rating.

feedback.en: Supply current capacity is not a current regulator for the LED. The higher applied voltage still changes current through the resistor.

text.en: Raise the wattage rating but keep the resistance, since the LED drop sets the current.

feedback.en: The approximately fixed LED drop leaves more voltage across the same resistor. Current rises as well as heat, so wattage alone is not the complete check.

text.en: Recalculate resistance but keep the old wattage rating, since current control also establishes safe heat dissipation.

feedback.en: Current-setting resistance does not by itself establish a safe wattage rating. Check power dissipation at the new operating point.

explanation.en: A resistor chosen for one supply is not automatically suitable when the supply changes.
